name: Deuel
overview: Deuel is a male member of the tribe of Gad, noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Eliasaph. His mention is brief but significant within the genealogical records of the tribe. There are no additional personal notes or events recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Deuel means 'known of G-d [El],' reflecting a recognition or acknowledgment by God. This proper name, as recorded in Numbers 1:14, is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theistic connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Deuel is explicitly identified as a descendant of the tribe of Gad and is the father of Eliasaph, as stated in Numbers 1:14. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Deuel's significance lies in his role within the genealogical framework of the tribe of Gad, serving as a link in the lineage through his son Eliasaph. This connection situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribal organization and census during the wilderness period. While not a prominent figure in terms of narrative action, his mention preserves the heritage and continuity of God's chosen people.
